# Release Notes: Hypercolor 0.3.0

**Released:** 2026-08-10

This release brings **interactive input**, **cross-platform screen capture**, and a **portable device identity** system to Hypercolor. Effects can now react to keyboard and mouse in real time, screen content feeds ambient lighting on both Windows and Linux, and devices survive hardware swaps with durable identity. The web UI gains a mobile-responsive shell, and the renderer adds GPU-accelerated area sampling via summed-area tables.

## ✨ Highlights

### Interactive Input Pipeline
Effects can now react to keyboard presses, mouse movement, button clicks, and scroll wheel input. A new `InteractionData` model delivers per-frame event batches with physical-position key names (W3C `KeyboardEvent.code` semantics) that map identically across QWERTY, AZERTY, Dvorak, and other layouts. Three capture backends feed the same data model: **evdev** on Linux, **Raw Input** on Windows, and **browser injection** over WebSocket for UI previews. Consent is controlled at runtime via `set_interaction_capture_active()`, and the system reports per-source health with degradation codes when access is restricted.

### Screen Capture on Windows and Wayland
New `hypercolor-windows-capture` crate implements Desktop Duplication (DXGI) screen capture with three reduction paths: zero-copy GPU surface handoff, compute-shader GPU reduction, and deterministic CPU fallback with rayon parallelism. On Linux, the Wayland backend uses XDG Desktop Portal with PipeWire streams and session restore tokens. The capture coordinator handles admission control, pooled staging textures, letterbox detection, temporal smoothing, and HDR/SDR color space resolution.

### Portable Device Identity
Devices now carry typed, cryptographically-grounded identity claims (`PortableDeviceKey`) derived from USB serial descriptors, MAC addresses, Hue bridge IDs, or Nanoleaf serials. These keys survive cable moves, OS reinstalls, and machine migrations. A new `device-aliases.json` store persists pins across restarts. When hardware is replaced, a REST API (`GET /devices/bindings`, `POST /devices/rebind`) lets users reassign layout bindings to the new device, migrating settings automatically.

### GPU Summed-Area Table Sampling
The SparkleFlinger renderer adds `gpu_area_sat.rs` with hierarchical GPU-accelerated area sampling for screen-capture zones. The implementation defines 6 compute pipelines (4 base tile/block passes for horizontal and vertical axes, plus 2 hierarchy pipelines) that dispatch across multiple hierarchy levels. At typical resolutions (1080p through 8K), the hierarchy produces **10 total compute dispatches**: 4 base passes plus 3 horizontal hierarchy passes plus 3 vertical hierarchy passes. This replaces per-pixel point sampling with exact integral averaging across arbitrary zone shapes.

### Mobile-Responsive Web UI
The Leptos web UI adds a bottom tab bar for phone-width viewports with safe-area padding for notched displays, glassmorph backdrop styling, and accent-colored active indicators. Settings reorganizes into horizontal tabs (General, Behavior, Connectivity, System) with scroll-spy section tracking and `?focus=` deep-linking. Legacy pages (Displays, Assets, Layout) are removed; Studio is promoted to a permanent navigation destination. Modals now portal-mount at `document.body` to escape stacking context issues.

### Effect Cover Artwork
All 41 bundled effects now ship inline cover artwork as base64-encoded WebP data URIs embedded at build time. Covers render at 960px width (WebP quality 88) to support high-DPI cards without upscaling. The `sync-covers.ts` tooling captures screenshots from the daemon's compositor canvas and skips screen-reactive effects (ambilight, screen-cast, web-viewport) to prevent committing private desktop imagery.

## 🤖 Interactive Input

- Added `InteractionData` data model with `KeyboardData`, `MouseData`, and `InteractionBatch` carrying timestamped edge events, hi-res wheel accumulation, and motion aggregates
- Built a unified key inventory (`keymap.rs`) mapping evdev codes, Windows Set-1 scan codes, and media keys to canonical physical-position names
- Introduced `InputRoutingGraph` for source-to-effect routing with generation-versioned availability tracking
- Added `BrowserInputSource` for WebSocket-injected preview input, scoped per connection lifetime
- Created `hypercolor-windows-input` crate with Raw Input message pump, session lifecycle management, device enumeration, and double-delivery prevention
- Built evdev backend with udev rule generation (`70-hypercolor-input.rules`, `70-hypercolor-input-all.rules`) for device access
- Added source health primitives (`InputSourceHealth`) with denied resource counts and degradation codes
- Introduced `Keystrike` showcase effect: keyboard ripples mapped to QWERTY grid positions, click shockwaves at cursor, velocity-modulated pointer light, and palette rotation via scroll wheel
- SDK `@hypercolor/core` exports new `input/` module with `getInputData()`, `isKeyPressed()`, `getRecentKeys()`, and typed event helpers

## 🖥️ Screen Capture

- Added `hypercolor-windows-capture` crate with DXGI Desktop Duplication, D3D11 compute-shader reduction (`reduction.hlsl`), and CPU readback with box-filter downsampling
- Built `hypercolor-windows-gpu-interop` screen bridge for D3D11-to-wgpu texture handoff via D3D11on12
- Added arbitrary-resolution CPU reducer with rayon-parallel tile processing, zero-copy sampling geometry, and double-buffered output slots
- Implemented exact publication demand propagation: effects declare screen source requirements, the capture coordinator materializes only the workers and planes needed
- Added monitor enumeration API and capture settings UI with on/off toggle, monitor selector, and disclosure panel
- Built cadence scheduler that honors per-route timing during retries and idles configured sources when no effect needs them
- Added Wayland PipeWire format negotiation, portal restore-token persistence, and rejection/correction recovery
- Introduced `ScreenByteAdmissionCoordinator` for quota-based resource control across GPU and CPU paths
- Removed arbitrary canvas resolution ceilings; layouts now admit any addressable dimensions

## 🔧 Renderer and Spatial Engine

- Added GPU area sampling via summed-area tables (`area_sat.wgsl`, `area_hierarchy.wgsl`) with hierarchical prefix-sum scans and exact integral zone averaging
- Introduced transactional render resource preparation (`TransactionalRenderResourcePreparation`) for atomic layout activation
- Added GPU zone projection (`projection.rs`) to transform zone geometries on GPU
- Made surface pool allocation fallible with lazy materialization to reduce startup memory pressure
- Pooled CPU screen upload textures and bounded uploads by pipeline depth
- Added incremental CPU layer transform stepping to avoid per-frame recomputation
- Made renderer retain last-good scene after projection or sampling failures
- Replaced Windows renderer default from Vulkan to DX12 backend
- Added atomic layout updates with persistence coordination

## 📱 Web UI

- Promoted Studio to permanent navigation; removed legacy Displays, Assets, and Layout pages
- Added mobile bottom navigation bar (`MobileNav`) with fixed positioning, safe-area insets, and glassmorph backdrop
- Introduced `mobile_only` flag on nav entries for destinations whose desktop equivalent is a sidebar widget
- Redesigned Settings as tabbed sections (General, Behavior, Connectivity, System) with scroll-spy and `?focus=` deep-linking
- Consolidated dashboard telemetry into a single Performance strip with phase timeline
- Added `InputAccessBanner` component showing when interactive effects need host input access
- Added device deletion from the detail panel for simulated displays
- Switched modals to portal mounting at `document.body`
- Added `UiSetupHook` and `UiChromeFlags` extension seams for embedders
- Redesigned effect cards to resolve artwork by effect ID instead of slug guessing
- Added interactive preview WebSocket transport with connection-scoped render lanes

## 🔌 Device and Discovery

- Introduced `PortableIdentityClaim` with four identity sources: USB serial, MAC address, Hue bridge ID, Nanoleaf serial
- Added `device-aliases.json` persistence with collision detection and key quarantine
- Migrated `device-settings.json` to schema v2 with portable-key-first key resolution and live migration from legacy keys
- Added REST API for device rebinding (`GET /devices/bindings`, `POST /devices/rebind`) with settings migration and bus event notification
- Added `driver_inventory.json` for durable per-driver discovery hints
- Made connectivity reconciliation await completion instead of detaching fire-and-forget tasks
- Added background worker gate for discovery subsystem

## ⚡ Performance

- Made prepared effect pool commits allocation-free
- Reused transactional screen smoother state across frames
- Pre-opened exact GPU capture slots to avoid per-frame allocation
- Bounded Windows event queues without front drains
- Shared execution and encoding pools across preview lanes
- Cached unassigned fallback sampling plans
- Wrote CPU reduction results directly into publication slots
- Added descriptor-keyed GPU readback for Windows capture

## 🐛 Fixes

- Fixed Hue bridge connect deadline to budget the full handshake, not just the TCP connection
- Fixed Push2 MIDI pacing and bounded palette sysex to prevent firmware wedge
- Fixed ENE SMBus delays to send in-batch instead of fragmenting across transactions
- Fixed PawnIO SMBus polls to stop forcing onto the kernel sleep timer
- Stopped frame-encode threads from inheriting render-thread priority
- Fixed PulseAudio fallback to cpal when PulseAudio cannot respond
- Fixed Nanoleaf external control to stream to an injectable UDP port
- Fixed Windows installer to register the SMBus broker
- Made state file replacement atomic on Windows with proper filesystem identity handling
- Added cancellation-safe layout mutations with serialized persistence
- Stopped daemon from retiring scene transactions while render loop is paused
- Fixed slow-consumer WebSocket drops to summarize instead of logging each one
- Preserved unknown top-level config sections across saves

## 👷 Build and CI

- Added sccache sharing across worktrees with mode-aware wrappers
- Added Windows CI lane with input and capture integration tests
- Normalized working tree to LF via `.gitattributes` for Windows test asset reading
- Added `cargo-fmt-workspace.ps1` for Windows-safe workspace formatting
- Added CMake toolchain file for MSVC dynamic CRT alignment with Rust
- Upgraded Servo embedder stack to 0.4.0
- Switched to native Windows HID backend for HAL
- Gated Windows CI job off the Servo build path

## 📝 Documentation

- Added input capture consent and platform limits guide (`docs/content/guide/input-capture.md`)
- Added specs 71-75: interactive input pipeline, Windows host input, input/capture hardening, PipeWire metadata, mobile-responsive UI
- Rewrote all site documentation for cross-platform 0.3 coverage
- Updated all UI and TUI screenshots
- Added inline cover artwork workflow documentation

## Breaking Changes

- **Legacy UI pages removed**: The Displays, Assets, and Layout pages are gone. All device and zone management lives in Studio.
- **Device settings schema v2**: Settings migrate automatically on first access after the device proves its identity. No manual action needed, but downgrading to 0.2.x will ignore v2 settings (a `.pre-v2.bak` backup is created on migration).
- **Canvas resolution ceilings removed**: Arbitrary canvas dimensions are now accepted. Effects using hard-coded 640x480 assumptions should use normalized coordinates.
- **WebSocket protocol changes**: New frame types for interactive previews, chunked transport, and input events. Clients using the Python or TypeScript WebSocket bindings should regenerate from the updated `websocket-v1.json` protocol definition.

## Upgrade Notes

- **Linux users**: Install the new udev rules (`70-hypercolor-input.rules`) for keyboard/mouse capture. The `.deb` and install scripts ship them automatically.
- **Windows users**: The installer now registers the SMBus broker. Re-run the installer or `install-windows-hardware-support.ps1` to pick up the change.
- **SDK effect authors**: Effects that want input should add `input: true` to their manifest metadata. Import `getInputData()` from `@hypercolor/core/input`.
- **Python SDK users**: Regenerate the OpenAPI client; new models for `InputStatus`, `ScreenCaptureCapacityStatus`, and device bindings are included.
- **Config files**: Unknown top-level sections in `config.toml` are now preserved across saves. No action needed.
